title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 53-56): Grothendieck axiomatizes a poset (𝓕, ≤) of 'figures'. Irreducible figures are called atoms or 'multiplicités'. Axiom C1 provides the atoms. Axiom C2 says every figure F is the sup of its atoms, F = sup_{X∈F̄} X. Hence F ↦ F̄ (the set of atoms below F) embeds 𝓕 into P(M), with M the set of atoms, and turns sups into unions.

Corollary 2 on p.54 characterizes the image 𝓛 ⊂ P(M):
(a) if A ∈ 𝓛 and A_i ∈ 𝓛 with A_i ⊂ A, then ∪A_i ∈ 𝓛 (closure under bounded unions);
(b) each x ∈ M has a smallest member A_x ∋ x.

This page first states, then strikes out, a condition (c) ∅ ∈ 𝓕. The NB notes that (c) follows from (a)+(b) when M ≠ ∅ (take the empty union, bounded by some A_x), and that in all cases it is equivalent to (c') 𝓕 ≠ ∅.

The page then states the converse ('Remarque'). Let M be a set and 𝓕 ⊂ P(M) satisfy (a), (b), (c). Then:
1° (𝓕, ⊂) satisfies C1 and C2.
2° The irreducible objects are exactly the A_x, and x ↦ A_x is a bijection from M onto them.
3° x ∈ A ⇔ A_x ⊂ A. This is tautological from the minimality of A_x. So, identifying M with the irreducibles, Ā = {A_x | A_x ⊂ A} is A itself.

A marginal note concerns A∩B: 𝓕 is stable under binary (indeed nonempty) intersection, with the empty intersection requiring M ∈ 𝓕.

Finally M is regarded as ordered by ≤ (inclusion of A_x's, 'never by <'). Its elements are multiplicities and sub-multiplicities. Figures are identified with the corresponding sets of multiplicities, which are down-closed sets (made explicit on p.56).

In modern terms this is a Birkhoff/Alexandrov-type representation. 𝓕 is a 'locally complete' (bounded-complete) lattice of down-sets of the specialization preorder on M; the A_x are the principal down-sets ↓x, which are the completely join-prime elements. The purpose is to build the combinatorial skeleton of a tame 'analysis situs': figures as unions of irreducible 'multiplicities' (strata) ordered by incidence.
errors: Gap in 2°: x ↦ A_x is a bijection only if A_x ≠ A_y for x ≠ y, i.e. a T0-type separation condition. This does not follow from (a), (b), (c); for example 𝓕 = {∅, M} with |M| ≥ 2 gives A_x = M for all x. In the forward direction (M = atoms of a figure poset) this holds automatically, but the converse as stated needs this extra hypothesis, or else M must be replaced by its T0 quotient.
Point 1°/2° also tacitly uses that each A ∈ 𝓕 equals ∪_{x∈A} A_x (true by (b) and (a)); this is not stated but is immediate.

Marginal remark: A∩B ∈ 𝓕 follows automatically from (a)+(b), since A∩B = ∪_{x∈A∩B} A_x is bounded by A. Only the empty intersection requires M ∈ 𝓕. The note seems to say exactly this, so it is not an error.

ideas.what: Characterization of families of subsets closed under bounded unions with minimal 'neighbourhoods' A_x, recovering the abstract poset of figures via irreducibles
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff-type representation via completely join-prime elements; Alexandrov (finite-neighbourhood) topologies and specialization preorder; prime-algebraic bounded-complete domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937), Alexandrov (1937); for the bounded/'compatible' version, Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981, event structures)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. The 'multiplicités'/tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 but not this formalism.

ideas.what: Viewing irreducible figures ('multiplicités') as a poset ordered by ≤ and figures as down-closed sets of multiplicities
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / stratification poset of a stratified space; down-sets = closed unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; later the 'exit-path' poset viewpoint)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures) in spirit only

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms for figures are essentially those of a prime-algebraic coherent/bounded-complete domain: closure under bounded unions, with sups existing only for 'compatible' figures (p.56), every figure a sup of irreducibles, and irreducibles ↔ points. This is the configuration-domain of a prime event structure, as in Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel. He arrives at the same structure from tame topology. The link between event-structure/domain theory and combinatorial stratified-space foundations is not usually drawn.
missed.quote: x∈A ⟺ A_x⊂A ... si on identifie M à l'ens. des objets irréductibles de 𝔉, alors pour A∈𝔉, Ā={A_x | A_x⊂A} s'identifie à A lui-même
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor curiosity. It would let domain-theoretic tools (prime algebraicity, coherence) be applied to posets of strata, but the mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary lattice-theoretic representation (Birkhoff/Alexandrov style), with a small T0 gap. The only interest is that it forms part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic foundation of 'analysis situs' via figures and multiplicities.

Struck first line reads roughly: 'c) ∅∈𝔉 [⟺ (au vu de b), c'est dire que M ≠ ∅)]'.
'(jamais par < !)' may be '≺', but it is in any case a strict-order symbol.
The final parenthesis is roughly '(cl. par figure à l'une des [multiplicités] strictes?)' and remains uncertain.
